input.quote: All other liability is expressly waived and released as a condition of, and consideration for, the execution of this Agreement by the Servicer or the Marketing Agent, as applicable. Each of the Servicer and the Marketing Agent, severally and not jointly, will be liable only for its own willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence in performing its obligations under this Agreement.
input.rationale: The liability architecture sits at or above the fallback on its material terms, so we do not redline it. (1) Mutuality: Section 6.2(a) (Servicer/Marketing Agent, p0283) and Section 5.2(a) (Depositor, p0243) are parallel "liable only for specific obligations" waivers, and our entities have the additional benefit of Section 9.6 limited recourse (p0378, claims against Depositor/Issuer limited to the Depositor Transferred Property) and Section 9.7 (p0381-p0382). Our side's exposure is therefore effectively bounded while the counterparty's is not. (2) Cap basis: there is no monetary or fee-based cap anywhere in the document — searches for "exceed"/aggregate-liability language return no cap, and the Servicing Fee (p0975) is never used as a liability ceiling. The fallback's "12 months of fees" cap exists to floor Vendor exposure; here Cellco's exposure in amount is unlimited, which exceeds the fallback and benefits us, so we do not introduce a cap that would only weaken our position. (3) Carve-outs: because no cap exists, indemnification (Section 6.3, p0291-p0292), confidentiality/data-protection breaches (Exhibit A policies, p0146), gross negligence and willful misconduct all carry unlimited exposure, and gross negligence, bad faith and willful misconduct are the express standards of Servicer liability and indemnity. Minor shortfalls of the preferred wording — no general mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages (the only such bar, p0469, binds the arbitral panel), no USD 1,000,000 floor, and no express "payment obligations are not damages" statement — are noted rather than flagged; the first two are only meaningful alongside a cap, and none is a material failure of the fallback. We note for the record (outside this rule) that Section 6.2(a) limits Cellco's liability to willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence, excluding ordinary negligence; that is a standard-of-care point, is mirrored for the Depositor, and is market standard for this securitization structure rather than a cap deviation.
